repairs.value: The AI text combines Sechler’s qualified preference for annihilation with Clifton’s known-option objection, then adds a new procedural constraint: final loss is justified only after remediable epistemic barriers are removed and the relationship is unmistakably offered.

The AI synthesis turns Clifton’s mother analogy, one-nonbeliever test, and known-option reply into a cumulative probabilistic case, then extends them by connecting unequal epistemic access to salvation stakes and rejecting uncertainty-based goods when less costly alternatives exist.
